title: fix(service-automation): a notify node naming email and another channel mails an unheld written-out address and writes no inbox row for it
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X1vxQ5eGqwz99QtDkLa1w1V)_

Fixes #25990

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

The sibling of #25758 (PR #25964), under the card's ruling: on a `notify` node naming both `inbox` and `email`, a written-out address no user holds goes to the email channel only, the inbox writes no row for it, and the node still succeeds. Identity: claim `6412253095` (branch `claude/project-thread-puin6e`).

## What changed

| `notify` node with `channels` naming `email` and another channel | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| written-out address no user holds, bare | mailed, AND a `sys_inbox_message` row whose `user_id` is the address; success | mailed only, no inbox row; success |
| `user:ADDRESS` (any address, held or not) | same junk row (the resolver hands the remainder on as the id with no lookup) | mailed only; success |
| address whose holder cannot be looked up (no data engine, lookup throws) | junk row + mail; success | mailed only; success |
| written-out address a user holds, bare | that user's inbox + mail | unchanged |
| computed address on a mailing node | resolved to its user, or the node fails (ruling-B screen) | unchanged |
| node without `email` | fails on an unheld address (#25964) | unchanged |

- `service-automation` `notify-node.ts`: new `mailOnlyAddresses` collects the written-out recipients only the email channel can deliver, using the exact test `refuseUndeliverableAddresses` (#25964) makes, now shared as `holderOf` (the `sys_user` by `email` lookup, id projected, system read) and `namesAddressAsUserId` (the `user:` rule). `screenComputedAddresses` and `refuseUndeliverableAddresses` call the same `holderOf`, so there is one address test in the file, not a second resolver.
- When the node mails and names another channel, `execute` emits those recipients apart with `channels: ['email']`, and every other recipient as before on the node's `channels`. `notificationId` names the every-channel notification (the one the inbox shows) when there is one; `delivered`, `enqueued` and `failed` add up both emits. A node with no such recipient makes exactly the one emit it made before.
- The `recipients` help served to the Studio inspector says what such an address does.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: the new test's `findOne` double, written by `check:engine-double-contract --write`.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/service-automation` `patch`.

## Where the skip lives (PM hypothesis, measured)

In the node, not the inbox channel. Measured on `main` `b0384f3f`:

- `EmitInput` (`service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts:75`) carries ONE `audience` and ONE `channels` list; there is no per-recipient channel restriction a producer can pass, so a node-side skip is two emits, and a messaging-side skip would be a new field on the service contract.
- `RecipientResolver.resolveEmail` keeps an unheld address verbatim on purpose ("a downstream channel may still key a row by it"), and the inbox channel keys `user_id` by whatever recipient it receives. Making the inbox refuse a non-id would change what `user_id` means to that channel for every producer (`collab.mention`, audit writers, any `emit`), and on the outbox path it would still enqueue a `sys_notification_delivery` row that then fails.
- The node is the one place that knows a recipient was WRITTEN OUT as an address and which `channels` its author named, so the skip is there, and every channel and the resolver keep their one meaning of a recipient.

## Is it a narrowing (measured against AGENTS.md)

No. Every node that succeeded still succeeds and every node that failed still fails: the split runs only after the parse, the ruling-B screen and the #25758 refusal have answered, and it only chooses which channels an address is handed to. No key, value or stored shape moves and the parse is unchanged, so `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`. The claim carried `Clause-②: yes (expected: … unchanged; the dev measures)`; measured, the accept set is unchanged in both directions, so the line is `no` with no arm.

## Tests

- New `notify-both-channels-unheld-address.integration.test.ts` (7 cases), real `MessagingService` (inline fan-out), real inbox and email channels, data engine recording every row: bare unheld address, `user:ADDRESS` unheld and held, a list beside a user (inbox row for the user only, both mailed, `selected: 2, acted: 3`, two `sys_notification` events), a directory lookup that throws; controls: a held bare address reaches its user's inbox and is mailed, a computed held address reaches its user's inbox.
- **Red first** (commit `da686d76`, before the fix, on `main` `b0384f3f`): 5 failed (each on the inbox row whose `user_id` is the address), the 2 controls passed.
- **Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, one behaviour: the `mailOnlyAddresses` call replaced by an empty set; the test imports the node from `src`, no `dist` in the path): 5 failed, 17 passed across this file and `notify-written-address-channels.integration.test.ts` (the 5 are exactly the fixed cases). Restore: blob `e7907826` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Verification

Under the verify lock, at `1ce55062` (the ledger pin `745715539` after it changes no source):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation test`: 205 files / 2689 passed; `typecheck` (with `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config packages/services/service-automation`: exit 0.
- Derived gates (`dispatch-gates --commands`, 76 families on the final diff): 75 exit 0; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 PREREQUISITE NOT MET (needs a full-repo build; CI runs it). Reconciled with `--ran`: 76 accounted, 0 unrun.
- Open PRs on `notify-node.ts`: none found (open-PR search on `notify` / `service-automation`, 2026-10-26T10:02Z).

## Acceptance notes

- A run whose recipients mix users and such addresses now writes two `sys_notification` events for one node (users on the node's `channels`, addresses on `email`). The node's output keeps its keys; `notificationId` names the first. If the second emit throws after the first was accepted, the node fails with the users' notification already written: a partial outcome one emit could not have. `emit()` throws only before its fan-out (a malformed keyed text, an event write the engine refuses), and both emits carry the same input, so the second refusing after the first was accepted needs the engine to change its answer between them.
- The rule covers every channel beside `email`, not only `inbox`: on a node naming `email` and `sms`, such an address is no longer handed to sms, where it used to be a failed delivery (`no phone number for recipient`), so `failed` drops by one for it.
- `@objectstack/spec` describe text for `recipients` (`io-node-config.zod.ts`) does not say what a both-channels node does with an unheld address; that is the `domain:spec` text, not in this PR.
